core_functions.description: The alpha5 chain supplies type-IV collagen protomer and terminal-domain interfaces, contributing basement-membrane network architecture and mechanical integrity. Alpha5-containing protomers are distinct from fibrillar collagens. Human recombinant NC1 self-assembly supports intrinsic structural participation without equating its homohexamer crystals to the native alpha3/alpha4/alpha5 network or assigning collagen the enzymes that modify and crosslink it.

followup.core_criterion: A reproducibly measured isolated-domain molecular activity remains a valid proposed annotation, but does not by itself establish a primary conserved role for core synthesis. Endogenous alpha5 fragment identity and physiological role remain unresolved. No denial of intact-chain activity or in-vivo requirement for binding annotation.

30.reason: GO:0030199 concerns processes determining collagen-fibril size and arrangement, not a requirement that every participant itself be a fibrillar collagen. The available PMID:29853175 abstract describes fibril assembly generally but does not resolve a COL4A5-specific contribution; bounded original full-text recovery was unsuccessful. Type-IV network identity and the recombinant NC1 assembly evidence in PMID:30443360 neither establish this exact fibril-organizing role nor exclude effects on other collagen fibrils. Retain source-specific uncertainty without converting absent access into evidence against the preserved NAS assertion.

35.reason: The actual solid-phase assay coats recombinant human NC1 (reported Gly1461–Thr1685) or pentastatin and adds alpha1beta1 integrin, detected through beta1, with BSA and random-peptide controls. Cellular crosslinked immunoprecipitation corroborates association. This is not binding of isolated beta1 monomer or proof that intact matrix collagen and both full-length products have the same accessible activity. The 20-residue sequence maps to canonical1510–1529 and isoform2 1516–1535; reported peptide coordinates do not establish which whole isoform was assayed. NC1-reactive tissue/ELISA signals do not identify a naturally liberated 20-residue peptide. The current cell-matrix-adhesion child is not required by these binding/barrier assays; no existing annotation or replacement is an ancestor/descendant of this MF. This is retained as a measured fragment activity, without elevating it to a primary core function while the endogenous product and role remain unresolved. The family-level Reactome:R-HSA-2327695 summary mentions type-IV collagen binding and alpha1/alpha2/alpha3 NC1 ligands, but does not independently establish an alpha5-specific intact-chain or released-fragment mechanism.
